mainTopic: רבי מאיר's קנס for מזיד vs. שוגג, and who gets the שבח (improvement) on a stolen item and how it is paid.
overview: The amud opens by asking whether רבי מאיר's קנס applies only to someone who acts on purpose (מזיד) or also to someone who acts by mistake (שוגג). A proof from a stolen field is pushed off, because the buyer there may have been a תלמיד חכם who knew the land was stolen. The משנה about a dyer who used the wrong color then proves that רבי מאיר penalizes only a מזיד. Next the גמרא asks what the difference is between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about a stolen item that gained value. רב זביד says they argue whether that improvement belongs to the owner or to the גזלן. רב פפא says both give it to the גזלן, and they argue only whether he gets all of it or just a worker's share. A משנה about a pregnant cow seems to challenge רב פפא, but he answers it, and a ברייתא supports him. רב אשי then reports a question: is the גזלן's share paid in money or in meat? It is answered from שמואל's rule that improvement is paid in money. That rule leads רבינא to challenge שמואל's statements about a בעל חוב, and רב אשי's final answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How the buyer of a stolen field gets his money back
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא about a robber who sold a stolen field. The buyer collects the purchase price from the robber's sold property, and the improvement only from his unsold property, because the real owner took both the land and its improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The buyer collects the principal from the robber's liened (sold) property, and the improvement from his free (unsold) property, because the owner of the land came and took his land and its improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that it began quoting just before this point, as a possible proof about רבי מאיר's קנס. Here we learn how the buyer of a stolen field collects from the robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real owner takes back the field and also the improvement the buyer added. So the buyer has lost two things, and he goes back to the robber for both: the price he paid (קרן) and the improvement (שבח). The key detail for the next step is that the owner gets the שבח too, which looks like a penalty on the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, meaning the price the buyer paid for the field
The improvement, the extra value added to the field
Liened property, land the debtor already sold to others that a creditor can still collect from
Free property, land still owned by the debtor and not sold
The owner of the land

phrases.english: He collects the principal
from liened property,
phrases.notes: The robber's land that he already sold to other people.

phrases.english: and the improvement from free property.
Because the owner of the land came
and took his land and its improvement.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹבֶה אֶת הַקֶּרֶן מִנְּכָסִים מְשׁוּעְבָּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting before this section as a test case for רבי מאיר's קנס.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי מאיר penalizes even a שוגג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a stolen field sold to a buyer who improved it

steps.title: Trying to prove that even a mistaken buyer is penalized
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is talking about an ignorant buyer who did not know land can be stolen. If so, he acted by mistake, and still lost the improvement. That would prove רבי מאיר penalizes even a שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this talking about an ignorant person who doesn't know whether land can be stolen or not? And even so, the landowner comes and takes the land and its improvement. So we learn that he penalizes even someone who acted by mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now draws a proof from the ברייתא. It says the buyer was probably an ignorant person who acted innocently, yet he still lost the improvement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עם הארץ might think that once he bought the field it was really his, so he did nothing on purpose. If even he must give up the שבח, the קנס must apply to a שוגג too. The proof depends on assuming the buyer was ignorant.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not? A way of offering a reading of a source in order to prove something
An ignorant person who does not know the halacha
Land can be stolen (in the legal sense)
Someone who acts by mistake, without knowing he is doing wrong
He penalizes, imposes a קנס

phrases.english: What, is it not about an ignorant person
who does not know whether land can be stolen
or cannot be stolen,
and even so the owner of the land comes
and takes the land and its improvement,
so learn from this: he penalizes even someone acting by mistake?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו בְּעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling in Step 1 (owner takes the שבח) to build a proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר penalizes even a שוגג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, read as talking about an ignorant buyer who still loses the שבח

steps.title: No proof: the buyer was a scholar who knew
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The ברייתא can be talking about a buyer who is a תלמיד חכם and knew the land was stolen, so he acted on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. It is talking about a buyer who is a תלמיד חכם, and he knew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the ברייתא as talking about a buyer who knew he was buying stolen land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer knew, he is a מזיד, and penalizing a מזיד tells us nothing about a שוגג. So this source cannot settle the question, and the גמרא tries a new source in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The buyer
A Torah scholar

phrases.english: They say: No;
it is about a buyer who is a Torah scholar, and he knew.
phrases.notes: He knew the robber had no right to sell this land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא; בְּלוֹקֵחַ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 2 by changing who the buyer is.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof, not the idea itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא does not have to be about an ignorant buyer; it can be about one who knew, which makes him a מזיד.

steps.title: A new source: the dyer who used the wrong color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a dyer was told to dye wool red and dyed it black, or the opposite. רבי מאיר says he pays the value of the wool. The גמרא reads this closely: only the wool's value, not the added value from the dye.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he was told to dye it red and he dyed it black, or black and he dyed it red, רבי מאיר says: he gives him the value of his wool. The value of his wool, yes; the value of his wool and its improvement, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new source to answer the question. This step sets up the case and the exact wording the next step will use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dyer went against the owner's instructions, so רבי מאיר makes him pay. But he pays only for the wool as it was, not for the higher value the dye added. That small detail is what the proof will rest on.

keyTerms.meaning: To dye
The value of his wool
Yes

phrases.english: Come and hear: to dye it red for him
and he dyed it black,
black and he dyed it red,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he gives him the value of his wool.
The value of his wool, yes;
the value of his wool and its improvement, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: לִצְבּוֹעַ לוֹ אָדוֹם וּצְבָעוֹ שָׁחוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי מאיר penalizes a שוגג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the dyer, read closely: wool's value yes, improvement no

steps.title: Why the dyer case shows no penalty for a mistake
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר penalized even a שוגג, the dyer would have to pay the wool plus its improvement. Since he does not, it seems רבי מאיר penalizes only a מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think he penalizes even someone acting by mistake, he should have to give him the value of his wool and its improvement! Rather, must we not learn from this: on purpose he penalizes, by mistake he does not penalize?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof from the dyer case and asks whether the conclusion is that only a מזיד is penalized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא treats the dyer here as someone who made a mistake. If the קנס applied to a שוגג, he would lose the שבח just like the buyer in the field case. Since רבי מאיר lets him keep the שבח, the קנס must be only for a מזיד.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind, meaning if you assume this
To give
Rather, is it not so? Introducing the conclusion of a proof
Someone who acts on purpose, knowing it is wrong

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that he penalizes even someone acting by mistake,

phrases.aramaic: דְּמֵי צַמְרוֹ וְשִׁבְחוֹ בָּעֵי לְמִיתְּבָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he should have to give him the value of his wool and its improvement!
Rather, must we not learn from this:
on purpose he penalizes, by mistake he does not penalize?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בְּשׁוֹגֵג נָמֵי קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the wording in Step 4 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר penalizes only a מזיד, not a שוגג
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dyer pays only the wool's value, not the שבח

steps.title: Conclusion: the penalty is only for acting on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: learn from this that רבי מאיר penalizes only a מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the field case, which could be pushed off, the dyer case stands. So the הלכה in רבי מאיר's view is: קנס for a מזיד, no קנס for a שוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's קנס (losing the שבח) applies only to someone who acts on purpose (מזיד). The field case did not prove otherwise, because that buyer was a תלמיד חכם who knew. The dyer case shows that a שוגג is not penalized.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof offered in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר penalizes a מזיד but not a שוגג.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון from the ברייתא and asks what the practical difference between their views is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a stolen item is returned as it is. רבי שמעון says: we look at it as if it had been priced in money while with the גזלן. What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא, quotes two more opinions about a stolen item that changed while with the גזלן, and asks what practical difference there is between them. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance both opinions seem to say the same thing: the גזלן gives back the item, and the owner does not pay him for the improvement. So the גמרא asks where they would actually give different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: A stolen item (taken by force or openly)
Is returned as it is, in its current form
A price set by appraisal
What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A stolen item is returned as it is.
Rabbi Shimon says:
We view it as though it
was priced in money while with him.
phrases.notes: He means: treat it as if the item was valued in money at the moment it was stolen.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי מאיר and turns to the other two opinions in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case where רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון would rule differently.

steps.title: רב זביד: They argue about who owns the improvement still on the item
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says they argue about improvement still on the stolen item: רבי יהודה says it belongs to the owner, רבי שמעון says it belongs to the גזלן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: They argue about improvement that is still on the stolen item. רבי יהודה holds it belongs to the one who was robbed, and רבי שמעון holds it belongs to the גזלן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers the question: the argument is about an improvement that is still part of the item when it is returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Returned as it is' (רבי יהודה) means the owner gets the item with the improvement, and the גזלן gets nothing for it. 'Priced in money' (רבי שמעון) means the owner gets only the value from the time of the theft, so the improvement belongs to the גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: Improvement, added value
That is still on the stolen item itself
The one who was robbed (the owner)
The robber

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
They disagree about improvement that is on the stolen item –
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
It belongs to the one who was robbed,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
It belongs to the robber.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: בְּשֶׁבַח שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי גְּזֵילָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is ownership of improvement still on the item: the owner according to רבי יהודה, the גזלן according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב פפא: They argue about whether the robber gets all of it or only a worker's share
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says both agree the improvement on the item belongs to the גזלן; they argue whether he takes all of it or only a half, third or quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Everyone agrees that improvement still on the stolen item belongs to the גזלן. Here they argue about a half, a third or a quarter. רבי יהודה holds that all of the improvement belongs to the גזלן, and רבי שמעון holds that the גזלן takes only a half, a third or a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer to the same question. In his view, both agree that the גזלן gets the improvement, and they argue only about how much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב זביד, רב פפא does not say the owner keeps all of the improvement. According to רבי יהודה the גזלן gets all of it. According to רבי שמעון he gets only part of it, like a worker who raises someone else's animal for a share.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
For a half, a third or a quarter (a share of the profit)
Takes

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch: according to רב פפא, it is רבי יהודה who gives the גזלן ALL of the improvement. That is the opposite of how רב זביד read רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Everyone agrees:
Improvement that is on the stolen item –
belongs to the robber;
and here they disagree about a half, a third and a quarter –
phrases.notes: These are the usual shares a worker gets for raising someone else's animals, depending on local custom.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Improvement that is on the stolen item –
all of it belongs to the robber,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
a half, a third or a quarter
is what the robber takes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא, שֶׁבַח שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי גְּזֵילָה – דְּגַזְלָן הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב זביד's answer and offers another explanation of the מחלוקת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both agree the improvement goes to the גזלן; רבי יהודה gives him all of it, רבי שמעון only a worker's share.

steps.title: Bringing the משנה about a stolen cow and ewe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if someone stole a cow that became pregnant and gave birth, or a ewe that grew wool and was sheared, he pays the value at the time of the theft.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: If someone stole a cow, and it became pregnant with him and gave birth; or a ewe, and it grew a load of wool with him and he sheared it, he pays according to the time of the theft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to begin a proof about how to understand the מחלוקת. This is setup: the key reading of the משנה comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases of the משנה, the improvement (the calf, the wool) has already been separated from the animal. The משנה says the גזלן pays only what the animal was worth when he stole it.

keyTerms.meaning: Became pregnant
Became loaded (with wool)
According to the value at the time of the theft

phrases.english: We learned in a Mishna:
If one stole a cow, and it became pregnant with him
and it gave birth;
a ewe, and it became laden with wool with him
and he sheared it –
he pays according to the time of the theft.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: גָּזַל פָּרָה, וְנִתְעַבְּרָה אֶצְלוֹ וְיָלְדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to test the two explanations of רב זביד and רב פפא.
steps.raayaObject: The explanation of the מחלוקת (it will support רב זביד).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of גזל פרה ונתעברה אצלו.

steps.title: Reading the משנה: if the cow did not yet give birth, it is returned as is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: only if the cow gave birth does he pay the old value; if it did not give birth, the cow goes back as is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it gave birth, yes, he pays the old value. If it did not give birth, the cow is returned as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the exact wording of the משנה, which says 'and it gave birth.' This builds the proof that will be completed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions birth for a reason: only once the calf is born does the גזלן just pay the old value. While the cow is still pregnant, the improvement is still on the item, and it goes back 'as is,' improvement included. That matches the language of רבי יהודה, which fits רב זביד's view that the owner gets improvement still on the item.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
It is returned as it is

phrases.english: If it gave birth – yes,
if it did not give birth – it is returned as is;

steps.triggerLanguage: יָלְדָה – אִין, לֹא יָלְדָה – הָדְרָא בְּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the משנה quoted in step 10 closely to build the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's view that improvement still on the item goes back to the owner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The close reading of 'וילדה' in the משנה: no birth means the cow returns as is, improvement included.

steps.title: The משנה fits רב זביד but seems to fit no one for רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The reading of the משנה from step 11 (the cow goes back as is) works for רב זביד as רבי יהודה's view. According to רב פפא, though, the משנה matches neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רב זביד, who says that for רבי יהודה improvement still on the stolen item belongs to the owner, our משנה follows רבי יהודה. But according to רב פפא, who says the improvement belongs to the גזלן, whose view is our משנה? It is neither רבי יהודה nor רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inference from the משנה to challenge רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that if the cow is still pregnant, it goes back to the owner as is, and the גזלן gets nothing for the improvement. רב זביד says רבי יהודה holds exactly that. רב פפא says both תנאים give the גזלן at least part of the improvement, so the משנה seems to match nobody.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well for
Improvement or added value
The person who was robbed, the owner
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Zevid, who says:
improvement that is still on the stolen item
belongs to the one who was robbed, according to Rabbi Yehuda;
whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: 'This' is our משנה, read the way step 11 read it: the pregnant cow goes back as is.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא, דְּאָמַר: דְּגַזְלָן הָוֵי –
phrases.english: But according to Rav Pappa, who says it belongs to the robber,
whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן!
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yehuda, and not Rabbi Shimon!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference made in step 11 to test both explanations
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that both תנאים give the improvement to the גזלן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies the still-pregnant cow goes back as is, with no share for the גזלן. That contradicts both views as רב פפא explains them.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'gave birth' was only written to match the first case
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that even if the cow did not give birth, the גזלן pays its value at the time of the theft. The משנה only says 'gave birth' in the second case because it said so in the first case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא could tell you: the same is true even if it did not give birth. He still pays the value at the time of the theft. The משנה says 'gave birth' only because the first case used 'gave birth', so the last case used it too.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends himself by taking away the inference from the משנה's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on reading 'gave birth' as a real condition. רב פפא says the word is not exact in the second case; it was only copied over to match the first case. Without the inference, the משנה no longer says the pregnant cow goes back as is, so it no longer contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: The same rule applies
Since it already used this wording
The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the word 'gave birth' is extra in both cases. It matters in the first case; it is only in the second case that it was copied over for style.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ לֹא יָלְדָה נָמֵי –
phrases.english: The same is true even if it did not give birth:
he pays according to the time of the theft,
and the fact that it teaches 'gave birth'
is because the first part used 'gave birth',
phrases.notes: The first part is the משנה's first case: a cow that was already pregnant when it was stolen.

phrases.english: so the last part used 'gave birth' too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the inference: the wording is not exact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Gave birth' is a real condition, so a cow that has not given birth goes back as is
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Gave birth' in the second case only matches the first case; even without birth the גזלן pays the value at the time of the theft

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying the stolen animal is treated as if it had been valued in money, and the גזלן gets a half, a third, or a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב פפא: רבי שמעון says, we look at it as if it had been valued in money while with him, and he gets a half, a third, or a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב פפא's explanation of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רב פפא said the argument is whether the גזלן gets all of the improvement or only part of it. This ברייתא shows רבי שמעון giving the גזלן a half, a third, or a quarter. That is exactly the 'part of it' view רב פפא described.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in support of him
An appraisal, a value set in money
For a half, a third, or a quarter

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in support of Rav Pappa:
Rabbi Shimon says:
We view it as though it were
appraised in money while with him,
phrases.notes: Picture an animal handed to someone at a set price to raise, with a share in whatever it gains.

phrases.english: for a half, a third, or a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב פפא, the גמרא adds outside support for him
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that רבי שמעון gives the גזלן only part of the improvement
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון: a half, a third, or a quarter
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, everyone agrees the improvement goes to the גזלן. רבי שמעון gives him only a share (a half, third, or quarter), and a ברייתא supports this.

steps.title: רב אשי: does the robber get his share in money or in meat?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports a question asked in רב כהנא's study hall. According to רבי שמעון, when the גזלן is paid off for his share, does he get money, or does he take part of the animal's meat?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall, we were asked: According to רבי שמעון, who says the גזלן takes a half, a third, or a quarter, when we pay him off, do we pay him off with money, or perhaps he takes from the meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new practical question that builds on רבי שמעון's view from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know the גזלן gets a share of the improvement, the question is how that share is given. One option is that he is paid its value in money. The other is that he takes his share from the animal itself, from its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: We were asked a question
We remove him, pay him off
With money
From the meat

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
When we were in the study hall of Rav Kahana,
we were asked:
According to Rabbi Shimon, who says

phrases.aramaic: לְמֶחֱצָה, לִשְׁלִישׁ וְלִרְבִיעַ הוּא דְּשָׁקֵיל גַּזְלָן,
phrases.english: that the robber takes a half, a third, or a quarter,
when we remove him,
phrases.notes: He means: when we take the animal back and give the robber his share.

phrases.english: do we remove him with money,
or perhaps he takes from the meat?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי הֲוֵינַן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא, אִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי שמעון's view in the ברייתא and asks how it works in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the גזלן's share under רבי שמעון is paid in money or taken from the animal's meat

steps.title: The question is answered from שמואל's three cases
steps.stepSummary: The question about the גזלן's share is answered from שמואל's rule. In three cases, improvement is valued and paid back in money: a בכור to a regular brother, a בעל חוב to a לוקח, and a בעל חוב to יתומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We answered the question from what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל. In three cases the court values the improvement for the people who made it, and they are paid in money. These are the cases: a בכור paying a regular brother, a בעל חוב paying a לוקח, and a בעל חוב paying יתומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. It shows from שמואל's rule that the person who improved something gets paid in money, not with a piece of the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each of שמואל's three cases, someone improved property that ends up with another person, and he is paid back with money. The גמרא uses this to settle the question. The גזלן is also paid for his share in money, not by taking part of the animal's meat.

keyTerms.meaning: we resolved (the question)
improvement, added value
they value it, they appraise it
they pay them off with money
firstborn son
creditor, the lender

steps.whatToRemember: The question is settled. Someone who improved property in these cases gets money for the improvement, not a share of the property itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question from step 15 about רבי שמעון's view. The גזלן's share is paid in money.

phrases.english: And we resolved it from this
phrases.notes: "It" is the question from רב כהנא's study hall about how the גזלן gets his share.

phrases.english: that Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
In three cases, they value the improvement for them,
and they are paid off with money;
and these are they: a firstborn to a regular son,
and a creditor to a buyer,
and a creditor to orphans.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְשַׁטְנָא מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Improvement is paid in money, so the גזלן gets money for his share, not part of the meat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the גזלן is paid in money or in meat.

steps.title: רבינא: Doesn't שמואל say the creditor collects the improvement?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how שמואל could say that a בעל חוב pays the לוקח for the improvement. שמואל himself said that a בעל חוב collects the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Did שמואל really say that a בעל חוב gives the לוקח payment for the improvement? But שמואל said that a בעל חוב collects the improvement!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא points out that two statements of שמואל seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the list from step 16, the בעל חוב has to pay the לוקח for the improvement. But in another statement, שמואל says the בעל חוב takes the improvement too. It cannot be both, so רבינא asks which one is right.

keyTerms.meaning: buyer (here, someone who bought land from the borrower)
collects
but didn't he say? (raising a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: The case is a borrower who sold his land to a לוקח, and the בעל חוב then takes that land to collect his debt. The question is who gets the improvement the לוקח made.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Did Shmuel really say

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל חוֹב לְלוֹקֵחַ יָהֵיב לֵיהּ שֶׁבַח?
phrases.english: that a creditor gives the buyer the improvement?
But didn't Shmuel say:
A creditor collects the improvement!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, מִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second case in the list of שמואל quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a בעל חוב pays the לוקח for the improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction: שמואל elsewhere rules that a בעל חוב collects the improvement.

steps.title: Ripe improvement versus unripe improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the two statements deal with different kinds of improvement. When the produce is ripe and ready to carry on the shoulders, the לוקח is paid for it. When it is not yet ripe, the בעל חוב collects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about improvement that reaches the shoulders, and there it is talking about improvement that does not reach the shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי solves the contradiction by showing that each statement of שמואל is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Improvement that "reaches the shoulders" means the produce is fully grown and ready to harvest and carry. In that case, the לוקח is paid for it. If the produce is not ready yet, the בעל חוב takes the improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
here... and there (two different cases)
improvement that reaches the shoulders: produce that is ripe and ready to carry

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not difficult.
Here, it is about improvement that reaches the shoulders,
phrases.notes: This is the case where the לוקח gets paid: the produce is ripe enough to pick and carry on your shoulders.

phrases.english: and here, it is about improvement that does not reach the shoulders.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּשֶׁבַח הַמַּגִּיעַ לִכְתֵפַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's contradiction from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each statement refers to a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two statements contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ripe improvement is paid to the לוקח; unripe improvement is collected by the בעל חוב.

steps.title: But in practice שמואל collected even ripe improvement
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects that cases came up every day, and שמואל had the בעל חוב collect even ripe improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But there are cases every day, and שמואל has the creditor collect even improvement that reaches the shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's answer using what שמואל actually did in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said that ripe improvement goes to the לוקח. But in real cases שמואל let the בעל חוב collect even ripe improvement. So רב אשי's answer seems to go against שמואל's own practice.

keyTerms.meaning: cases that happen every day, real practice
has someone collect, lets him collect

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא מַעֲשִׂים בְּכׇל יוֹם,
phrases.english: He said to him: But there are cases every day,
and Shmuel has the creditor collect
even improvement that reaches the shoulders!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָא מַעֲשִׂים בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's split between ripe and unripe improvement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's practice in real cases goes against the split: he let the בעל חוב collect even ripe improvement.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a new answer
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי replies that there is no difficulty. His explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב אשי says there is no contradiction, and the גמרא will give his explanation right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not give up his position. He signals that he will show why שמואל's practice fits with his rule. The actual reason comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not difficult;
